detail.abstract: This paper studies the sociodemographic and economic characteristics linked to vaccine hesitancy in the MENA region. The paper uses a dataset developed by the World Bank based on a large scale phone survey which collected attitudes towards the Covid-19 vaccination. Using a logit model and marginal effects, I find that in the MENA region the willingness to vaccinate is positively associated with: age, being a male, living in urban areas, greater institutional trust, and the perception that many individuals were impacted by COVID-19 in their community. Knowledge of these underlying determinants of vaccine hesitancy can enable policymakers to design more targeted interventions for specific demographic groups and reduce health inequalities.

title: Holder Fallibility: A Framework for Understanding Cryptographic Asset Succession Failure

detail.title: Holder Fallibility: A Framework for Understanding Cryptographic Asset Succession Failure
detail.abstract:
We introduce "Holder Fallibility" as a theoretical framework for analyzing a critical market failure in cryptographic asset ownership: the absolute dependency on a single individual's ability to produce a private key or seed phrase (Access Credential) to control digital assets. This dependency creates three distinct failure states: lost Access Credentials, holder incapacity, and holder death. An estimated $140+ billion in Bitcoin alone has been permanently lost through these mechanisms, with the problem scaling proportionally as tokenized real-world assets approach a projected $1.3 trillion market by 2030.

We examine nine categories of existing approaches—from informal key sharing through dead man's switches, multisignature wallets, information escrow, social recovery, seed phrase recovery, biometric authentication, custodial platforms and traditional estate planning—demonstrating no positive correlation between technical sophistication and legal compliance. Notably, biometric authentication is least effective during holder incapacity because it conflates authentication (identity verification) with authorization (legal right to act), requiring the holder's physical and cognitive participation at the moment of transaction.

We present a comprehensive risk taxonomy encompassing estate law violations, tax liability under the new IRS Form 1099-DA regime, criminal exposure, fiduciary liability, privacy risks, and the crypto-illiterate fiduciary problem. Case law analysis from four jurisdictions—the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, and Australia—confirms that courts uniformly classify digital assets as property subject to estate administration.

We propose that comprehensive solutions require integration of established legal structures (inter vivos trusts) with professional custody mechanisms supported by smart contracts, and present a trust-based framework comprising three structures differentiated by trust property designation—the wallet, the private key, or the custodial service provider account—each addressing specific custody arrangements across the full self-custody to custodial delegation spectrum. The framework has significant implications for institutional adoption, regulatory design, and the economic viability of blockchain-based asset markets.

title: Pricing Macro-Panic: Forecasting the Tails of Bond Risk Premia

detail.title: Pricing Macro-Panic: Forecasting the Tails of Bond Risk Premia
detail.abstract: Moving beyond conventional mean-targeted forecasts, I predict the entire distribution of bond risk premia to capture extreme, crisis-driven tail movements. Augmenting standard predictors with an extracted upper-tail macroeconomic factor-representing a latent "macro-panic"-achieves full predictive dominance over baseline models across the quantile spectrum. Methodologically, a Quantile Random Forest (QRF) efficiently captures non-linear crisis thresholds using mean-selected predictors, offering a computationally tractable, high-performing alternative to Quantile LASSO. The resulting forecasts exhibit pronounced regime-dependent cyclicality, becoming heavily countercyclical during recessions. Crucially, this approach reveals a term-structure duality: short-term tail risks are driven by acute macro-liquidity panics ("dash for cash"), whereas long-term risks are anchored by structural safe-haven demand ("flight to safety"). Finally, I document a decay in macroeconomic predictability along the yield curve: while the QRF dominates at shorter maturities, naive empirical quantiles become highly competitive at the long end.

title: Who Wins and Who Loses In Prediction Markets? Evidence from Polymarket
affiliations: , HEC Montreal - Department of Finance,  and University of Toronto - Rotman School of Management and UTSC Management

detail.title: Who Wins and Who Loses In Prediction Markets? Evidence from Polymarket
detail.abstract: We study trading gains and losses on Polymarket, the world's largest prediction market platform, using a comprehensive dataset of more than 1.4 million users from 2022 to 2025, totaling over $20 billion in volume across 70 million trades. We document a striking profit concentration: the top 1% of users capture 84% of all trading gains. Gains flow almost entirely to sophisticated traders who outperformed market-implied probabilities. Long-shot betting drives loss concentration, while market-making strongly predicts positive performance. Our results suggest that the informational benefits of prediction markets come at a cost to unsophisticated participants.

title: Multidimensional Analysis of Economic Transitions: Connecting Socio-Ecological Systems frameworks and Input-Output analysis in the tourism sector
affiliations: University of York, University of York, University of York and University of York

detail.title: Multidimensional Analysis of Economic Transitions: Connecting Socio-Ecological Systems frameworks and Input-Output analysis in the tourism sector
detail.abstract: Addressing the rising tide of environmental crises and social inequalities requires rethinking our economic models. This is a major challenge which requires holistic analysis that can address the multi-dimensionality of a wide range of possible economic futures. In this study, we develop a novel integrate the qualitative Socio-Ecological Systems scenario framework with quantitative Input-Output Analysis. To demonstrate the potential of this method, we use the East of England coast as a case study, developing four scenarios of transitional economic futures and analysing them across nine quantitative impact categories: compensation of employees, employment, gross value added, greenhouse gas emissions, qualifications, employment gender, opportunities for career progression, regulatory quality, and voice and accountability. Our findings show that scenarios centred on technology and infrastructure boost economic metrics but degrade environmental quality and risks governance quality. We also identify scenarios that reduce the environmental impact of tourism and address social inequities despite incurring economic decline, and highlight differences in governance structures These results underscore the importance of adopting holistic analytical frameworks to better inform decision-making and guide future economic transitions.

title: Government Positions and Climate Change: Paradigmatic Conflict vs. Consensus in Environmental Performance
affiliations: University of Greifswald

detail.title: Government Positions and Climate Change: Paradigmatic Conflict vs. Consensus in Environmental Performance
detail.abstract: Historically, environmental policy was framed as a fundamental trade-off between economic growth and ecological preservation. Since the mid-1980s, however, this dichotomy has been largely replaced by the paradigm of ecological modernization, which posits that economic growth and environmental protection are mutually reinforcing through concepts like "green growth" and "sustainable development." This shift was accompanied by the assumption that a broad political consensus on these concepts would lead to superior environmental outcomes. Yet, the persistent gap between climate targets and actual emission trends necessitates a critical re-evaluation of this "consensus" approach.,This study empirically examines the impact of ideational positions on climate performance across 36 advanced industrialized democracies from 1990 to 2021. Contrary to the consensus hypothesis, the results demonstrate that governments adopting antagonistic positions on the environment-growth dimension achieve significantly faster reductions in greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions than those holding moderate or consensus-oriented positions. These findings suggest that the depoliticization of climate policy may hinder transformative action, whereas ideological contestation—specifically regarding growth-centric paradigms—appears to be a key driver for effective emission reduction.

title: Institutional Friction Decomposition of Valuation Discounts: A Structured Diagnostic Framework for Identifying Institutional Sources of Persistent Discount Rate Distortions
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Institutional Friction Decomposition of Valuation Discounts: A Structured Diagnostic Framework for Identifying Institutional Sources of Persistent Discount Rate Distortions

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This paper presents a theoretical and analytical framework and does not involve the collection or processing of human subjects data. Accordingly, no ethics approval was required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract:
Contemporary asset-pricing models explain variation in security values primarily through expected cash flows and discount rates. A substantial body of empirical research, most prominently associated with John H. Cochrane's work on discount rate variation, demonstrates that movements in discount rates account for a large share of observed asset price changes. Yet prevailing models treat discount rates as functions of market beta, factor exposures, and return volatility, almost never modelling the institutional or structural complexity that shapes firm-level uncertainty.

Recent empirical work also provides independent confirmation that firm-specific discount rates are poorly captured by factor models, and that substantial cross-sectional variation in those rates remains unexplained by standard accounting variables. This paper argues that the source of that explanatory failure lies in a disciplinary blind spot: the risk premium is the financialization of perception, and perception formation is first and foremost a human capital and organizational legitimacy problem before it is a financial one. The result is that the observed risk premium performs two jobs simultaneously, pricing systematic risk and pricing institutional friction, with standard models seeing only the first.

This paper proposes Institutional Friction Decomposition (IFD), a diagnostic framework that audits the hidden institutional assumptions inside valuation models and maps their violation onto five mechanism categories: liability allocation, regulatory jurisdiction, audit verification depth, rights dependency, and path dependence. Each mechanism category corresponds to a distinct channel through which institutional uncertainty enters the discount rate, including tail-risk exposure, regime uncertainty, information asymmetry, property-rights fragility, and structural irreversibility. IFD sits at the intersection of asset pricing, institutional economics, corporate governance, regulatory economics, behavioral economics, and human capital theory. The framework provides a structured method for identifying which institutional mechanism constitutes the binding constraint on value, and for estimating the remediation path that would unlock multiple expansion.

The current framework is present at the firm level, and reflects a prior analytical framework concerned with national and market-level institutional frictions. Empirical validation, including an event-study design built on the Hommel, Landier, and Thesmar (2025) imputed IRR methodology, is proposed as the next step.

title: The case for collective autonomy in work time reduction research
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The case for collective autonomy in work time reduction research
detail.abstract: Work time reduction (WTR) is a policy that has been actively studied over the past decades. Existing research commonly frames its benefits through a ”triple dividend” of economic, social, and environmental gains. While empirical studies provide substantial evidence of individual-level benefits - such as improved well-being, better work–life balance, and reduced stress - less attention has been paid to the broader societal implications of the potential of WTR to foster collective forms of social organization, democratic participation, and community engagement. Drawing on the degrowth literature, this article makes a case for collective autonomy as an essential dimension of WTR research. The article argues that WTR can function as an enabling condition for collective practices to emerge. The article contributes to the conceptual development of WTR’s potential as a tool for fostering collective autonomy, and outlines a research agenda for interdisciplinary research to advance the knowledge of the collective dimension in reducing work time.

title: Know its worth? Factors affecting the social acceptability of water reuse: A mixed methods planned behavior model
affiliations: University of Toulouse and Aix-Marseille University

detail.title: Know its worth? Factors affecting the social acceptability of water reuse: A mixed methods planned behavior model
detail.abstract: In the current context of strong demographic pressure, rapid urban development, and climate change water demand is increasing while usable freshwater supplies are being depleted. The reuse of treated wastewater (RTWW) is one of the avenues currently being explored to ensure the quantitative and qualitative security of the water supply. The interests for social acceptability emerged with risk management approaches and the subsequent debates on the role of technical progress, the implementation of major development projects, and their consequences for the environment between the late 1970s and early 1980s. The purpose of this article is to identify the factors that influence the construction of RTWW acceptability. This study was carried out in southern France. It combines a quantitative survey on behaviour related to engaging in RTWW based on Ajzen’s theory of planned behaviour, with a qualitative socio-economic study aimed at understanding representations and beliefs regarding RTWW. The findings show that a lack of knowledge about RTWW and the current absence of projects result in a normative gap and a perceived lack of control. In addition, trust in managers and public authorities, the quality of treatments, as well as risks perceptions – particularly those relating to health – significantly influence intentions to engage in RTWW. Lastly, several factors such as emotions, types of uses, and environmental awareness play an underlying role by helping build perceptions of water reuse, trust in relevant stakeholders, and more accurate perceptions of risks.

title:
Pay Now, Buy Never: 
The Economics of Consumer Prepayment Schemes
affiliations: China Europe International Business School (CEIBS), China Europe International Business School (CEIBS) and University of Michigan at Ann Arbor

detail.title:
Pay Now, Buy Never: 
The Economics of Consumer Prepayment Schemes
detail.abstract: Prepaid consumption is a common feature of modern consumer markets and is often presented as a mutually beneficial arrangement: consumers receive upfront discounts, and firms secure future sales. We analyze a large-scale Pay Now, Buy Later (PNBL) program in which consumers prepay for restaurant credit with bonuses, and spend the balance later. Using detailed transaction data from over 4 million consumers, we document widespread balance breakage: approximately 40% of prepaid value is never used. Because many consumers underutilize their balances, merchants recover significantly more than the bonus cost. The median firm earns roughly $5.5 in breakage profit for every $1 of bonus credit issued. While PNBL participation does lead to modest increases in consumer spending over time, firms gain substantially more from breakage than from any loyalty-driven revenue. These findings challenge the prevailing win–win narrative: PNBL schemes often result in a significant transfer from consumers to firms. We develop a stylized contract model to illustrate the misaligned incentives firms face, and show through counterfactual analysis that a simple escrow policy with an appropriately chosen deposit requirement can realign firm incentives and generate more consumer-serving outcomes.

title: Maps and Territory: The Authority Paradox—Organizational Design and the Suppression of Capability
affiliations: Human Resonance Systems Research Collective

detail.title: Maps and Territory: The Authority Paradox—Organizational Design and the Suppression of Capability
detail.abstract:
Organizations operating in Gulf economies claim commitment to developing nationals while structurally perpetuating their invisibility and constraining their authority. This paradox is not accidental—it is organizational design in operation.

This paper examines how organizational structures simultaneously enable external consultants to build visible authority while preventing similarly capable nationals from advancing or building organizational visibility. The mechanism is subtle but powerful: authority is concentrated in external roles, decisions are outsourced to external expertise, knowledge is not systematized or transferred, and when nationals demonstrate capability, organizational structures prevent that capability from becoming visible or building authority.

Organizations experience a legitimacy crisis they sense before they understand. The crisis emerges from fundamental contradiction: stated commitment to nationals meets structural reality that prevents their advancement. For Gen Z workforce entrants now prioritizing social mobility and equitable opportunity above compensation, this contradiction creates recruitment, retention, and talent attraction challenges that threaten long-term organizational viability.

The paper demonstrates that outsourcing authority to external consultants appears economically rational in the short term—it transfers responsibility, risk, and cost. But this choice creates organizational brittleness. When external consultants leave, capability leaves with them. When external expertise is unavailable, decisions cannot be made. When organizations cannot access external validation, their judgment capability becomes paralyzed. Organizations become dependent on permanent external presence for operational decision-making.

The paper proposes specific organizational transformation pathways: redistributing authority to nationals, systematizing knowledge transfer through structured mentoring, creating advancement transparency through capability-based criteria, and building organizational judgment capability through distributed decision-making. These pathways enable organizations to simultaneously develop national capability and build organizational resilience.

The analysis integrates organizational design theory, knowledge transfer research, and organizational behavior evidence to show that different organizational structures produce different outcomes. Organizations can be deliberately redesigned.

For organizational leaders, the paper presents a strategic choice: maintain current authority outsourcing patterns and accept long-term organizational brittleness and legitimacy loss, or transform organizational structures enabling nationals' capability visibility and organizational capability building.

Keywords: Organizational design, authority distribution, capability suppression, legitimacy crisis, knowledge transfer, organizational transformation, human capability, organizational autonomy

title: Maps and Territory: Capability Suppression -Individual Capability Recognition, Agency, and Collective Power in Gulf Talent Systems
affiliations: Human Resonance Systems Research Collective

detail.title: Maps and Territory: Capability Suppression -Individual Capability Recognition, Agency, and Collective Power in Gulf Talent Systems
detail.abstract:
This paper addresses a critical paradox in talent development systems: capable individuals are systematically prevented from advancing and building authority despite demonstrated capability. Through analysis of individual experience within systemic institutional constraint, the paper demonstrates that capability suppression is not a consequence of individual limitation but of organizational and policy design.

The paper identifies three key mechanisms of suppression: (1) assessment systems measuring organizational conformity rather than job-required capability; (2) advancement criteria favoring credentials and background rather than demonstrated performance; and (3) visibility and recognition systems concentrating public acknowledgment for external professionals while internal excellence remains invisible. These mechanisms operate simultaneously, creating psychological internalization where individuals absorb system narratives and develop self-doubt despite objective evidence of capability.

However, the paper demonstrates that individuals retain agency within systemic constraint. Drawing on self-determination theory and individual agency frameworks, it identifies how individuals can refuse narratives, document capability, build visibility, and organize collectively. The paper provides concrete action frameworks and documents cases where nationals successfully navigated out of suppression through individual and collective action.

The analysis bridges individual agency theory with systemic institutional analysis, showing how personal power and collective action can transform systems designed to maintain capability invisibility.

title: How Neuroscience and Emotional Identification Shape Consumer Psychology
affiliations: GEMS Dubai American Academy

detail.title: How Neuroscience and Emotional Identification Shape Consumer Psychology
detail.abstract: In this modern world, companies' marketing teams have shifted from observing external consumer behaviours to analysing internal neurological triggers, trying to maximise the consumers' brain chemistry and years of evolution. This paper explores the integration of neuroscience; especially the roles of the prefrontal cortex and the limbic system: the behavioural and emotional brain structures, with the emotional identification strategies in contemporary marketing. By examining how brands utilize mirror neurons and dopamine pathways, the research demonstrates that purchasing decisions are often the result of subconscious emotional resonance rather than rational utility. The findings suggest that emotional identification acts as a primary driver in brand loyalty, effectively bypassing the prefrontal cortex which controls the consumers' logic, and influencing long-term consumer habits.

title: Selling Professional Products with Consumer Uncertainty in Expertise Advancement
affiliations: University of Connecticut - Department of Marketing, University of Science and Technology of China and University of California, Davis - Graduate School of Management

detail.title: Selling Professional Products with Consumer Uncertainty in Expertise Advancement

declarations.declarationOfInterest: NA
declarations.ethicsApproval: NA
declarations.funderStatement: NA

detail.abstract: (1) Problem definition: For professional products such as musical instruments and sports gear, a consumer's quality preference is positively associated with the consumer's expertise level. A novice who initially chooses a low-quality product over a high-quality one may have incentive to upgrade if experiencing expertise advancement after professional training. This paper examines a firm's strategies to sell professional products in two periods, training and post-training, between which consumers' expertise levels advance with uncertainty. (2) Methodology/results: Using a game theoretic model, we find that consumer uncertainty about expertise advancement allows the firm to expand product line and implement expertise-based intertemporal segmentation in selling a line of professional products. In addition, the firm can implement ex-ante market segmentation, selling products of different qualities to consumers with different quality preferences before their training starts. Our analysis reveals the innate conflict between these two types of segmentation so that the firm may forego the opportunity of market segmentation and implement intertemporal segmentation only. Interestingly, offering a trade-in credit facilitates intertemporal segmentation and encourages the firm to offer a product line, whereas a buyback program facilitates market segmentation instead. In addition, the total consumer surplus increases whenever trade-in credit enables upgrading, and otherwise deteriorates or remains the same. Finally, we find that the firm is more likely to offer a product line when selling to myopic consumers, and consumer myopia may hurt firm profit. (3) Managerial implications: Marketers of professional goods can strategically 2 facilitate and meanwhile profit from consumer upgrading. Also, whereas a buyback guarantee is commonly used in a regular goods market to cope with buyer uncertainty, a trade-in program is often a better option in a professional goods market.

detail.abstract:
This book examines the emergence of architectural advertising as a defining force in contemporary urban and cultural production. It argues that architecture—particularly in flagship stores, branded commercial spaces, and luxury retail environments—has evolved beyond functional and aesthetic concerns to become a strategic medium of branding, symbolic power, and spatial governance. Through qualitative case studies, visual-spatial analysis, and critical theoretical synthesis, the book demonstrates how branded architecture shapes consumer behavior, urban identity, and socio-cultural relations within global cities.

Integrating perspectives from urban theory, political economy, cultural studies, and postcolonial thought, the research introduces key concepts such as advertising migration and the Brand–Urban Assemblage Theory (BUAT) to explain how corporate branding, architectural form, and global networks interact across multiple spatial scales. The findings reveal a persistent tension between economic vitality and cultural homogenization, highlighting the ethical challenges branded architecture poses to public space, local identity, and urban equity. The book contributes a critical framework for understanding architecture as a socio-political instrument in the contemporary capitalist city.

title: Maps and Territory: The Regulatory Vacuum—Knowledge Transfer Systems and Equitable Advancement in Gulf Talent Policies
affiliations: Human Resonance Systems Research Collective

detail.title: Maps and Territory: The Regulatory Vacuum—Knowledge Transfer Systems and Equitable Advancement in Gulf Talent Policies
detail.abstract:
Why do Gulf talent acquisition systems perpetuate external expertise dependency despite two decades of explicit policy commitment to developing nationals and building regional knowledge economy capability? This paper reveals the answer: a regulatory vacuum that enables systemic perpetuation mechanisms to absorb policy pressure without changing fundamental operation.

Through mechanism-level institutional analysis, the paper identifies five core mechanisms perpetuating external dominance and three regeneration mechanisms that explain why policy interventions targeting outputs are rendered ineffective. The critical finding: compliance-based policy is absorbed into organizational structures without changing the underlying mechanisms that prevent nationals from advancing or capability from transferring. Organizations appear to comply while continuing to operate according to unchanged design principles.

The paper demonstrates that transformation is achievable but requires fundamentally different intervention. Rather than output-focused mandates, policy must intervene at the mechanism level across five dimensions: assessment system design that measures authentic capability, authority distribution that enables nationals to build visible authority, knowledge systematization that prevents expertise hoarding, organizational positioning that values nationals' contribution, and implementation speed justification that addresses economic extraction incentives.

The paper proposes concrete regulatory framework interventions, examining how policy mechanisms interact with organizational and individual constraints to enable actual systemic transformation. The analysis is grounded in comparative development evidence from Singapore and South Korea, which successfully transitioned from external expertise dependency to national capability leadership through systematic mechanism-level investment.

For policy-makers across GCC nations, the paper presents a strategic choice: maintain the regulatory vacuum enabling current patterns, or establish transparent regulatory frameworks aligned with stated policy objectives. With a $174.65 billion labor market projected by 2034 and global recognition of talent development as national security imperative, the economic and strategic case for transformation is clear.

Keywords: Talent acquisition, regulatory framework, policy implementation failure, Gulf Cooperation Council, knowledge transfer, institutional design, mechanism-based intervention, equitable advancement, policy effectiveness

title: AI Perception Index 2026 How Large Language Models Position Brands in the AI Era

detail.abstract: This report presents the first empirical measurement of brand perception across Large Language Models (LLMs) using the Perception Control Framework v2 (PCF v2). Six brands were analyzed across GPT-4o and Claude Sonnet using 8 standardized prompts. Key findings: a 36-point MPI gap exists between dominant and emerging brands; brands with $29M in funding score nearly identically to bootstrapped firms; and cross-model perception drift reaches 21.86 points for the same brand across different AI systems. These findings validate the Perception Control category — the discipline of measuring and managing how AI systems semantically represent brands.

title: AI as a Decision Partner: Transforming Consumer Purchasing Behavior and Ethical Challenges
affiliations: Islamic Azad University and Payame Noor University

detail.title: AI as a Decision Partner: Transforming Consumer Purchasing Behavior and Ethical Challenges
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), as a decision-making partner, transforms consumer purchasing decisions by leveraging advanced and real-time data processing to deliver personalized insights. Drawing on empirical data from global surveys and theoretical frameworks, we analyze how AI enhances product selection, pricing optimization, and purchase timing through predictive analytics and recommendation algorithms, while differentiating its impact on routine versus complex decisions. Key findings reveal AI's influence on increasing purchase frequency, product variety, and impulse buying, alongside shifts in preferences and reduced autonomy. However, its integration raises ethical concerns, including risks to consumer autonomy, privacy, and potential biases in algorithmic recommendations, which are analyzed to highlight the broader implications for consumers and society. By integrating practical insights and ethical considerations, this work contributes to the growing discourse on AI's role in consumer psychology and decision-making, offering directions for future research to balance technological advancements with consumer well-being.

title: Perception Control: A Foundational Category for an AI-Mediated Visibility Era

detail.abstract:
The emergence of Large Language Models as primary knowledge interfaces has fundamentally altered how entities are discovered, understood, and referenced. Traditional visibility strategies, designed for search engine environments, assume that ranking in a list of results defines success. This assumption no longer holds in AI-mediated discovery contexts.

This document introduces Perception Control as a foundational category for navigating this new environment. Perception Control is not a refinement of optimization. It is a categorically different approach: managing how AI systems interpret entities rather than how search engines rank pages.

This whitepaper defines the category, explains why it is distinct from SEO and GEO, and clarifies what Perception Control is and what it is not.

title: The Geometry of Monetary Circulation with Hidden Routing

detail.title: The Geometry of Monetary Circulation with Hidden Routing

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no known financial or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study does not involve human participants or personal data and therefore did not require ethical approval.
declarations.funderStatement: This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: We develop a structural theory of monetary circulation under partial observability. Money is modeled as a path-dependent semi-Markov process moving across an institutional network, where transfers are observed only at aggregated endpoints while part of the routing occurs through hidden or unrecorded channels. Rather than at- tempting to reconstruct unobserved flows, we characterize their observable imprint on the visible economy. We show that hidden circulation induces three robust ef- fects: (i) distortions of measured turnover and residence times, (ii) endogenous trapping and congestion not ex- plained by network topology alone, and (iii) systematic irreversibility that may remain invisible in observed flows. The key object is a phase field defined on visible links, inter- pretable as a directional shadow price of hidden circulation, orthogonal to incentive-based (potential) explanations. Irreversibility is formulated at the level of monetary paths via path-space relative entropy. We prove that entropy pro- duction in the observed economy is always a lower bound on true entropy production, with a nonnegative gap captur- ing hidden irreversibility. When the hidden phase contains a genuine cycle component and the economy uses that cy- cle, hidden entropy production is strictly positive even if observed circulation appears nearly reversible. We connect these structural results to macroeconomic out- comes by defining a price-free structural output proxy based on the interaction of monetary activation and directional circulation. Under stable institutional regimes, this proxy is shown to be affine-comparable to measured GDP growth. The framework provides a unified account of dark circulation, irreversibility, and macroeconomic inefficiency, without invoking equilibrium prices, representative agents, or welfare optimization. This paper completes a three-paper sequence by extending the framework to hid- den and partially observed circulation.

detail.abstract: The recruitment process today relies heavily on Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS), which often act as strict gatekeepers. Studies suggest that nearly 75% of qualified resumes are rejected by these systems, often due to simple formatting errors or missing keywords rather than a lack of skills. To address this issue, this paper proposes "JobFit-AI" a web application developed to help candidates navigate automated screening. The system is built using the MERN stack (MongoDB, Express.js, React, Node.js). Unlike traditional parsers that rely on basic keyword counting or Cosine Similarity, our approach integrates the Google Gemini API. This allows for semantic analysis, enabling the system to understand the actual context of a resume PDF when compared to a job description. Leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs), the application generates a "Fit Score," identifies missing skills, and offers specific suggestions for improvement. Testing indicates that this LLMbased method provides significantly higher accuracy than standard string-matching techniques, as it utilizes advanced prompting to interpret a candidate's true potential.

detail.abstract: Decentralised communities increasingly need ways to generate, contest, and maintain shared knowledge without relying on central editorial authorities. Existing collaborative systems such as wikis support large-scale knowledge production, but typically depend on centralised moderation and governance, while blockchain consensus mechanisms are primarily designed for transactional state rather than the validation and revision of shared claims. This paper introduces Pensieve, a framework for decentralised epistemic governance in collaboratively governed knowledge bases. Pensieve combines structured submissions, contribution-weighted support, and stake-backed dispute escalation to govern the publication, revision, and contestation of knowledge entries over time. The paper makes three contributions. First, it presents Pensieve as a framework for decentralised epistemic governance designed specifically for collaboratively governed knowledge bases rather than for transactional ledgers alone. Second, it formalises a contribution-weighted model of item governance and dispute resolution, showing how reputational participation and economic stake may be combined to support knowledge revision that remains both dynamic and increasingly stable over time. Third, it examines the Pensieve instance on ECF.network as an early live implementation context through which the framework is being applied to the collaborative documentation and evaluation of Web3 projects. The case study provides descriptive evidence that the framework can support structured publication, community contribution, dispute handling, and AI-assisted but human-accountable input in practice, while also revealing unresolved challenges around referencing, sustained participation, postpublication revision, and long-term governance design. Pensieve is therefore offered not as a completed solution to decentralised knowledge governance, but as a research framework and live design experiment for coordinating collective knowledge production in human-AI systems.
